the findings here (and in the other agent scenarios) disappear because the pinned conformance runner matches span definitions by the `gen_ai.<op>...<kind>` pattern, so it doesn't recognize `gen_ai.client.invoke_agent` and skips expected-attribute checks for it. That's also why the scenario runs report some `expected_violations` as "no longer reported".

#629 bumps the conformance pin to a version that supports both span type formats

None of the four scenarios emits the new metric's `error.type` attribute in its committed data; the added handlers have no demonstrated failed invocation. This leaves an added field without reference coverage, contrary to `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:41-43`. Add an expected SDK-failure case to at least one affected scenario and regenerate its data to demonstrate the error dimension.

threads.body: The pinned conformance policy's `_matching_span_type` requires `gen_ai.invoke_agent` as the prefix and `.client` as the suffix, so this rename disables its expected-attribute checks. Missing finish-reason and token-usage findings disappear from the committed results even though those attributes remain in the model. Update the policy and `CONFORMANCE_REF` to recognize the renamed type, then regenerate results and retain exceptions for attributes the providers cannot supply.

threads.body: The timed `client.interactions.create` call selects a model and conversation context, not a remote agent, so the new metric incorrectly counts inference as an agent invocation. `interactions_agent` is also neither passed to nor returned by the SDK, making the reported agent-name coverage unsupported. Exercise a real remote-agent invocation, or report this path as inference and remove the invented agent name from both span and metric attributes.

The new metric includes `server.address` but omits `server.port`. Its model inherits `attributes.gen_ai.address_and_port`, which requires the port whenever the address is set. The mock endpoint's port is available in `MOCK_LLM_URL`; include it so this reference emits the required metric dimension.

This timer combines run creation, application-owned tool execution, tool-output submission, polling, and message retrieval into one client operation. No single SDK invocation owns that interval, contrary to the library-API boundary required by `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:39`. Measure an SDK invocation or helper that owns the full operation, or omit this scenario's metric if no such boundary exists.

replies.body: Assistants runs can be one instrumentable call - `runs.stream(..., event_handler=handler)` with `until_done()`, where tool calls are handled in the handler callbacks. The conformance mock does not support Assistants streaming yet, so the scenario keeps the create/submit/poll flow for now. Mock streaming support: https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-conformance/pull/413; the scenario will switch to `runs.stream` once it is pinned.
